evidence.quote: Across all of these efforts, we are making significant investments in artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI, to improve our delivery, targeting, and measurement capabilities.

The increases in average price per ad in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools.
Changes in foreign exchange rates had an unfavorable impact on our revenue in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

input.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: The increases in average price per ad in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools.
Average price per ad in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 14% year-over-year.
Across all of these efforts, we are making significant investments in artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI, to improve our delivery, targeting, and measurement capabilities.

input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges, my initial SUPPORTED verdict remains correct.

H1 challenged whether ad targeting and measurement tools are linked to AI investments. E7 explicitly refutes this challenge by stating: "Across all of these efforts, we are making significant investments in artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI, to improve our delivery, targeting, and measurement capabilities." This directly connects AI investments to the targeting and measurement tools mentioned in E1.

H2 challenged whether other factors (currency, mix) drove the gains instead of ad performance improvements. This is refuted by the evidence. E1 explicitly states the increases were "driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools." While E1 mentions that foreign currency and mix shifts had some effects, it clearly identifies ad performance improvements as the primary driver. E10 confirms that foreign currency actually had an "unfavorable impact" on Q3 2026 revenue, meaning the advertising performance gains occurred despite currency headwinds, not because of them.

H3 sought evidence of negative impacts from AI investments on advertising performance. No relevant evidence was found to support this challenge.

The evidence review notes that E1 has a period mismatch, but this appears to be an error in the automated review. E1 explicitly discusses "the three months ended September 30, 2026," which is exactly the Q3 2026 period in the claim. The passage provides both the observed result (14% increase in average price per ad) and the stated cause (improvements to ad targeting and measurement tools), which E7 confirms are powered by AI investments.

The claim is SUPPORTED: Meta's Q3 2026 results show improved advertising performance (14% increase in average price per ad), and the filing explicitly attributes this primarily to improvements in ad targeting and measurement tools, which are powered by AI investments.
